Thanks again for the demo today — helpful session. Quick recap from our side and a couple of follow-ups so we can scope work on our end:

- We're evaluating Redwood for transaction enrichment and fraud-reranking (low-latency constraints).
- Primary concern: how to authenticate from our microservices (k8s) and from some 3rd-party batch jobs (air-gapped-ish).
- Preferations: service account model + short-lived JWTs if possible; also need support for rotating API keys and a clear audit trail for key use.

Questions:
1) Do you support OAuth2 service accounts / JWT-based tokens, or is it API-key-only today?
2) What rotation primitives are exposed (APIs, CLI, scheduled rotation)?
3) Can we scope per-environment keys (dev/staging/prod) and per-team scopes?

If you can share the integration guide and a sample flow for k8s auth, that’ll help our infra team estimate.

Next steps from our side: Priya will compile a short security checklist and Sam will coordinate engineer availability for a 30-min follow-up.

Thanks — Alex
Senior Infra Manager, FintechCo

Alex — great to meet you both today. Attaching our integration guide (PDF) and a proposed mutual action plan (Excel) to help your infra team estimate. High level answers below and a suggested follow-up for engineering: 30-min deep-dive with Dylan + Dev to walk traffic/rotation patterns.

Short answers:
- Redwood supports both API keys and OAuth2-style service accounts. We offer short-lived JWTs minted by our control plane (recommended for server-side workloads) and static API keys for legacy clients.
- Rotation: we expose a key management API (create/list/rotate/revoke), CLI tooling, and you can configure automatic rotation policies (e.g., rotate every 30/90 days). We also emit audit logs to your SIEM (via a push or S3 delivery) and surface events in the Console.
- Scoping: keys/service-accounts can be scoped by deployment (project/environment) and by role (ingest-only, read-only, admin).

Notes for k8s setups:
- Recommended: create a FintechCo service account in Redwood, generate a short-lived JWT (15 min — default) via the control-plane token endpoint, and use the Kubernetes TokenRequest or an init-container to fetch/refresh.
- For batch jobs in constrained networks, you can provision environment-scoped static keys and enable rotation via our CLI (rotate tokens automatically from a bastion host).

I'll loop in Dylan (runtime lead) and Dev (security engineer) to answer any implementation-specifics. Proposed times for 30-min follow-up: Wed 10/14 10:00–12:00 or Thu 10/15 09:00–11:30 PT. Which works for your engineers?

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Hi Priya + team — quick technical clarifications from our infra side:

1) KMS/HSM: Redwood does not require us to hold raw customer key material. We support customer-managed key (CMK) wrapping via Google KMS / AWS KMS — your keys can be used to encrypt the envelope keys we use; we can also integrate for signing JWTs if you want. We will provide an onboarding playbook for KMS binding.

2) Audit logs: configurable retention up to multiple years. We export logs to your S3/GCS bucket or push to your SIEM via secure delivery. For 13 months retention, we can set that in the Console or provide the export config.

3) Rotation primitives:
- API: POST /v1/keys (create), POST /v1/keys/:id/rotate (rotate), POST /v1/keys/:id/revoke (revoke), GET /v1/audit/events?key_id=
- CLI: redwood key create/rotate/revoke --project fintechco --env prod
- Recommended pattern: issue service-account-bound short-lived JWTs for all k8s microservices (15m–1h TTL), and use static environment keys only for air-gapped batch jobs with an automated rotate job (bastion host cron).

4) Service account mapping: we support OIDC and SAML-linked service accounts so you can map tokens to your identities.

I’ll bring a sample rotation script to the follow-up meeting (it’s a 30-line bash/python snippet). Confirming availability: Thu 10/15 10:00 PT works for Dylan and me.

— Dev
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
